readout.purpose: Transport clock and any live numeric value; teal, tabular-nums, mono.

readout-small.purpose: Fader percentage, pan value, clip name overlay.

label.purpose: Track names, button text, section titles.

shadows.name: active-glow-primary
shadows.purpose: Marks a genuinely live/armed control state (playing, soloed).

shadows.name: selection-ring
shadows.purpose: Marks the currently selected clip on the timeline.

components.name: Primary Button (Play)
components.description: Icon-only transport play/pause control; glows while playing.
components.html: <button class="ds-btn-icon ds-btn-primary" aria-pressed="true"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="currentColor"><path d="M6 4l14 8-14 8V4z"/></svg></button>
components.css: .ds-btn-icon.ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 36px; height: 36px; border-radius: 6px; background: #f97316; color: #1a0f04; border: none; box-shadow: 0 0 10px rgba(249,115,22,0.55); transition: background 0.15s; } .ds-btn-icon.ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #ea690f; } .ds-btn-icon.ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 1px solid #f97316; outline-offset: 1px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Default action button (Enregistrer, Exporter, Ajouter une piste).
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; height: 36px; padding: 8px 16px; border-radius: 6px; background: #2a2c31; color: #f0efec; border: none; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.3); transition: background 0.15s; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: rgba(42,44,49,0.8); } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 1px solid #f97316; outline-offset: 1px; }

components.name: Destructive Button (Recording)
components.description: Record toggle while recording is active; pulses.
components.html: <button class="ds-btn-destructive"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="currentColor"><rect x="6" y="6" width="12" height="12"/></svg> Arrêter l'enregistrement</button>
components.css: .ds-btn-destructive { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; height: 36px; padding: 8px 16px; border-radius: 6px; background: #ef4444; color: #200404; border: none; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; animation: ds-pulse 1.5s ease-in-out infinite; } .ds-btn-destructive:hover { background: rgba(239,68,68,0.9); } @keyframes ds-pulse { 0%,100% { opacity: 1; } 50% { opacity: 0.6; } }

components.name: LCD Readout Panel
components.description: Recessed panel showing the transport clock in mono teal, tabular-nums.
components.css: .ds-readout { display: inline-block; background: #0b0c0e; border: 1px solid #34363c; border-radius: 6px; padding: 4px 12px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-size: 14px; letter-spacing: 0.05em; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; color: #4dd0e1; }

components.name: Mute / Solo Toggle
components.description: Two-state hardware toggle switch used for per-track Mute and Solo; Solo-active reuses the primary accent, Mute-active uses the dedicated console-mute amber token (see Mute-Is-Amber Rule) so the two toggles are never confusable.
components.css: .ds-toggle { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 6px; height: 32px; border-radius: 6px; border: 1px solid #34363c; background: #0b0c0e; color: #9a9ca3; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; transition: background 0.15s; } .ds-toggle:hover { background: rgba(52,54,60,0.6); } .ds-toggle-mute-active { border-color: #f5b544; background: #f5b544; color: #241704; } .ds-toggle-solo-active { border-color: #f97316; background: #f97316; color: #1a0f04; box-shadow: 0 0 8px rgba(249,115,22,0.55); }

components.name: Channel Strip
components.description: Fixed-size hardware track unit: color edge, name row, volume/pan sliders, mute/solo row.
components.html:
Piste 1

components.css: .ds-strip { position: relative; height: 160px; width: 240px; background: #1c1d21; border-bottom: 1px solid #34363c; } .ds-strip-edge { position: absolute; inset: 0 auto 0 0; width: 6px; background: #f97316; } .ds-strip-body { padding: 8px 8px 8px 16px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 8px; height: 100%; } .ds-strip-name { font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; color: #f0efec; } .ds-strip-row { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; } .ds-track-fill { height: 6px; flex: 1; border-radius: 9999px; background: rgba(249,115,22,0.2); } .ds-strip-value { font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-size: 11px; color: #9a9ca3; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }

components.name: Timeline Clip
components.description: Waveform clip on the graticule timeline; inset toned block with mono label and drag handles.
components.css: .ds-clip { position: relative; height: 96px; width: 220px; background: #0b0c0e; border: 1px solid #34363c; border-radius: 6px; overflow: hidden; } .ds-clip-label { position: absolute; left: 6px; top: 4px; z-index: 1; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-size: 10px; color: #9a9ca3; background: rgba(17,18,21,0.7); padding: 0 4px; border-radius: 2px; } .ds-clip-handle { position: absolute; top: 0; height: 100%; width: 6px; background: rgba(255,255,255,0.1); cursor: ew-resize; } .ds-clip-handle:hover { background: rgba(255,255,255,0.25); } .ds-clip-handle-left { left: 0; } .ds-clip-handle-right { right: 0; }

components.name: Slider
components.description: Volume/pan slider used in channel strips; thin orange-filled track with circular thumb.
components.css: .ds-slider { position: relative; display: flex; align-items: center; width: 100%; height: 16px; } .ds-slider-track { position: relative; height: 6px; width: 100%; border-radius: 9999px; background: rgba(249,115,22,0.2); overflow: hidden; } .ds-slider-range { position: absolute; height: 100%; width: 66%; background: #f97316; } .ds-slider-thumb { position: absolute; left: 66%; width: 16px; height: 16px; border-radius: 9999px; background: #111215; border: 1px solid rgba(249,115,22,0.5); box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.4); transform: translateX(-50%); }

narrative.overview: Edito is built as a hardware mixing console: a charcoal chassis with brushed-panel surfaces, printed hairline seams between sections, and physical-feeling controls (faders, toggle switches, an LCD-style time readout) rather than webpage widgets pretending to be studio gear. The interface is dense, always-dark, and legible at a glance — every state (playing, recording, muted, soloed, saved) reads instantly from color and position alone, because the sole user reads it hundreds of times a session with no time to interpret ambiguity. The palette is disciplined to a single accent: console-orange for action and record states, teal reserved exclusively for meters and time readouts. Everything else is charcoal neutrals and hairline borders. Two type families do all the work — IBM Plex Mono for every numeric readout (time, percentages, pan values), IBM Plex Sans for every label — so a glance at a glyph's shape tells the owner whether they're looking at a value or a name before they've even read it.
keyCharacteristics: Charcoal chassis with brushed-panel surfaces and hairline seams (`border-studio-border`), never open whitespace
One accent color (console-orange) for action/record/selection state; teal is a reserved meter-and-readout color, never a general accent
Mono for numbers, Sans for words — no exceptions
Toolbar sections separated by physical 1px dividers (`h-6 w-px bg-studio-border`), not spacing alone
Flat, inset, and bordered surfaces stand in for shadows — this is a panel-and-seam world, not a lifted-card world

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Console-orange is the only color that means "action, recording, or active selection." If a new control needs an active state, it reaches for orange or it isn't done — a second warm accent (amber, red-outside-destructive, etc.) is a system violation, not a variant.

rules.name: The Meter-Only Teal Rule
rules.body: Teal (#4dd0e1 console-meter / #2a5a61 console-meter-dim) is reserved for the LCD time readout and waveform rendering. It never appears on an interactive control (buttons, toggles, links); if teal shows up on something clickable, that's a build defect, not a new use case.

rules.name: The Mute-Is-Amber Rule
rules.body: Mute's active state uses console-mute (amber, #f5b544 / foreground #241704), Solo's active state reuses the primary console-orange accent — the two toggles must never share a color. This is a deliberate, named exception to the One Accent Rule: it governs the Mute/Solo track-state toggle pair specifically, not action/brand color.

rules.name: The Digits-Are-Mono Rule
rules.body: Any value that changes at runtime or represents a measurement — time, volume percent, pan position, clip labels — renders in IBM Plex Mono with tabular-nums. Any value that names something — a track, a button, a menu item — renders in IBM Plex Sans.

rules.name: The Inset-Not-Lifted Rule
rules.body: Depth is conveyed by recession (console-inset wells for readouts, clip bodies, status pills), never by elevation. Nothing in this system casts a resting drop shadow to look "raised"; a shadow only ever appears as a live-state glow.

dos: Do put every runtime number and code value in IBM Plex Mono with tabular-nums; every label and name in IBM Plex Sans.
Do separate control groups within a toolbar or transport bar with a literal h-6 w-px bg-studio-border divider, not extra gutter.
Do use bg-console-inset for any recessed/LCD-like readout surface (clock, status pill, control well, clip body).
Do reserve the active-glow box-shadow (shadow-[0_0_Npx_rgba(249,115,22,0.55)]) for genuinely live/armed states (playing, soloed), not resting emphasis.
Do keep the channel strip at a fixed h-40 w-60 footprint; it is a hardware unit, not a flexible card.
Do use console-mute/console-mute-foreground for Mute's active state and primary/primary-foreground for Solo's active state — never swap them or let either toggle borrow the other's color.
donts: Don't introduce a second general-purpose action/brand accent color. Console orange is the only "this is active/actionable" color for buttons and brand controls; red is reserved solely for the recording-hazard state. (Does not apply to the Mute/Solo track-toggle pair — see the Mute-Is-Amber Rule.)
Don't use teal (console-meter/console-meter-dim) on anything clickable — it is a meter/readout color only.
Don't add a resting drop-shadow to imply elevation; depth in this system comes from recession (inset backgrounds) and hairline borders, never a lifted-card shadow.
Don't add uppercase, letter-spaced "kicker" or "eyebrow" labels anywhere — no label in the shipped build uses that treatment, and it doesn't belong to this instrument-panel voice.

Don't reach for a raw Tailwind color utility (e.g. amber-400, amber-500) for any new UI state. Every color used in a component must resolve to a declared token (console-mute, primary, destructive, etc.); an un-tokenized literal is a build defect regardless of hue.
